text: We tested whether restricting strong-model training to the most confidently weak-labeled examples improves weak-to-strong generalization, using gpt2-small as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student with a keep_fraction of 0.7. Across 3 seeds, the weak supervisor reached 0.64 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.91, while the confidence-filtered transfer run reached 0.63 accuracy (SE 0.02) and a PGR of -0.05 (SE 0.09). This sits below the baseline PGR of 0.16, so the filtering approach shows no advantage here; indeed the negative central estimate suggests the student recovered none of the gap between weak and strong performance, though with an SE of 0.09 the PGR interval is wide enough that little can be resolved either way. With only 3 seeds, these numbers should be read as preliminary and not as evidence about the method's general behavior. Replication with more seeds and additional keep_fraction settings would be needed before drawing conclusions.
